CS2-H-01.note: Deciding span: the ridge chemistry is 'peculiar enough to account for the restriction without help' — a range that needs nothing further said about it is self-explanatory. Only 'anomalous' is live (a narrow range does invite it), and it dies on 'without help'; 'provisional' inverts the time order (the view becomes tentative only after the trials) and 'immaterial' is dead on arrival. Two live options out of four is the weakness here, not the reasoning.

CS2-H-02.note: I disagree with the file's key (C, 'calculated'). The blank is licensed by the clause that immediately follows it — 'and the manuscripts encourage the description: whole passages are struck through, and the replacements are entered in a hurried hand.' A hurried hand and struck-through pages encourage 'impulsive'; they do not encourage 'calculated'. The 'Yet' then does what 'Yet' does: it turns the evidence against the received description. Under the file's key the sentence says the manuscripts encourage a description they undercut, and the 'Yet' clause introduces evidence that SUPPORTS the blank rather than opposing it — both connectives run backwards. The batch's own convention agrees with me: CS2-H-01 ('long treated as ___ ... Transplant trials complicated that view') and CS2-H-05 ('often described as ___, since ... The catalogue records something narrower') both put the CHALLENGED characterization in the blank. 'Calculated' is defensible only if you read the second sentence in isolation.

CS2-H-03.note: Deciding span: 'blocks that held policies were paced out and checked twice a year, while blocks that held none were sketched from the end of the street' — precision varies by block, i.e. unevenly distributed. 'Deliberately falsified' misreads economics as deceit, 'beyond verification' is contradicted by the twice-yearly checks, 'gradually eroded' invents a time dimension. Three dead distractors.

CS2-H-04.note: Deciding span: the charge is 'easy to test and, on the numbers, unfounded: every table in the appendix reproduces what the authors say it does' — a correspondence check, which is exactly what refutes misreporting. 'Overstates' is the strong trap because the text names overstatement in its last sentence, but 'The charge is better read as' explicitly separates the stated charge from that better reading; if the blank were 'overstates' the sentence would be circular and the charge would not be unfounded. On the author's own doubt: 'withholds' is NOT second-defensible. Absence is not visible in a check that the tables reproduce what is claimed for them, so 'easy to test' would not hold; the sentence speaks to fidelity, not completeness. It is the third-best option, not the second.

CS2-H-05.note: Deciding span: 'accept material from any donor' — lack of selectivity is indiscriminate, and the rebuttal's second half ('reject about half of what those stations send') confirms it by showing the curators do in fact discriminate. 'Exhaustive' is the one live distractor and glosses only 'no ceiling'. Same weakness as CS2-H-01: two live options, so the guess floor is 50 percent even for a solver who has not settled it.

CS2-H-06.note: Deciding span: 'a fact that the defense had already conceded in writing before the term opened' — cross-examining a witness on a conceded fact buys nothing, so the silence is economy of effort. 'A concession' is a genuine trap because the word is echoed in the deciding span itself, and it is ruled out by a second feature: the concession was made in writing beforehand, so the silence cannot be the concession, only its consequence.

CS2-H-07.note: 'Traceable' is the right register, and the deciding span is 'a reader can follow the disagreement from session to session' — a record that yields the course of a thing but not its substance. Against 'contentious': the blank is governed by 'render', which asks what the minutes DO with the dispute; contentiousness is a property of the dispute that the minutes neither make nor unmake, and choosing it leaves the entire second clause ('not one entry records what was said') doing no work at all. 'Unintelligible' is the other lure and is contradicted by the same 'can follow'. Both die to one sentence, so this is medium rather than hard.

CS2-H-08.note: Deciding span: 'differed from itself by less than the modern specification allows' — self-consistency is uniformity, and the 'what it excludes' is the batch-to-batch unpredictability of the previous sentence. 'Unremarkable' and 'serviceable' are baited by the 'faint praise' framing but neither is what the final measurement measures. One sentence decides it, no second feature needed.

CS2-H-09.note: Key span: sentence 2 poses the elevation dependence and sentence 3 measures it — 'the lowest sites lose more than half of each year's accumulation'. A is genuinely defensible: functionally, the cores DO qualify the protection argument the opening sets up, and a strong solver can argue the sentence's role is qualification. What rules it out is narrow — the opening claim is about burial RATE per hectare, which sentence 3 never disputes; what it disputes is retention. That is a one-word distinction ('rates') and I would not be shocked to see a good reader defend A.

CS2-H-10.note: Deciding span: 'each of the eleven proved to have taken water from the pump by a route he had not anticipated' — the apparent exceptions dissolve. B is the careless-reader option (it reads 'He found eleven' and stops) and is contradicted by the rest of the same sentence.

CS2-H-11.note: The single trailing clause IS enough, and for a reason worth keeping: 'nothing has been found wrong with the reasoning that produced the old account' flatly CONTRADICTS A's third limb ('argues that the method behind the old account was unsound'), while D's only sin against the text is omitting the underwater explanation. An asserted falsehood beats an omission every time, and that asymmetry is a clean, teachable separator. A is two-thirds right, which is what makes the item hard rather than unfair.

CS2-H-12.note: Deciding span: 'granted the charge and declined to act on it' — a two-part stance, and sentences 3-4 explain both halves. The key is indeed the vaguest option in the set, but vagueness does not make this easy on its own: B is falsified by 'declined to act', D inverts the order, and C ('restates the complaint in terms the author would accept') is the live one, half-true and dropping the refusal that the rest of the text exists to justify. It lands medium, not easy — but it is the item in this set whose key could be reached by elimination without understanding the reply.

CS2-H-13.note: Deciding span: 'the two figures are not in competition' — the disagreement was never real. A is the strong trap and turns on a fine distinction: 'could not determine which crew had measured correctly' presupposes there is a fact of the matter the review failed to settle, whereas the sentence denies the question exists. Ruled out by 'Neither definition is wrong', which is stronger than agnosticism.

CS2-H-14.note: Deciding span: the first sentence rules out wingspan, and 'What separates them is the shoulder joint' names the replacement. A is baited by the final sentence's high-speed film, but the film established the joint character, not the negative claim about wings — that is established by the same-wingspan observation in sentence 2.

CS2-H-15.note: B tracks all four moves: table, non-composing conversions, eighty years of reprinting, and the proposed explanation. Unlike CS2-H-11 the twin is separated by more than a trailing clause: D is wrong twice over — the text identifies the defect rather than denying it, and no charge of inaccuracy is ever reported as having been made, so D's third limb has no referent. That makes this the easier of the two twin-pair items.

CS2-H-16.note: Deciding span: 'a range wide enough that the growth reported in two of the last five years falls inside it' — the sentence sizes the problem and shows the size matters. A is the strong distractor because it is a true description of the text, just of the FOURTH sentence ('Nobody proposes discarding the counts'); sentence 3 itself pushes the other way. B is a location trap (the cause is sentence 2). Two well-built positional traps.

CS2-H-17.note: C is the only option that carries both of Text 2's mechanisms — 'the hospitals with the fewest vacancies' and 'error logs ... filled in by whoever notices the error'. A imports fatigue, which Text 2 never mentions; B overstates ('at all'); D is recommendation-shaped and advises rather than responds.

CS2-H-18.note: Deciding span: the displaced carbon 'turns up again at forty to sixty centimeters, below where the corers stop'. C is the inversion trap and is contradicted by Text 2's own first clause, 'Plowing does not destroy carbon; it moves it.' B is fabricated.

CS2-H-19.note: Deciding span: 'A policy that helps chiefly the unaffiliated newcomer is worth having. It is not the policy the journals believe they have adopted' — grant the effect, deny the evenness. D is the best-built distractor and is directionally backwards: because a reviewer 'in a small field can often name the author', concealment bites LESS in small fields, so the effect should be smaller there, not larger. Worth keeping precisely because it punishes a solver who does not check direction.

CS2-H-20.note: Deciding span: 'the range across the structure settles well below the range measured in the open channel' — the quantity Text 1 squares is destroyed by the act of exploiting it. On the author's doubt: D is NOT a second key. Two independent features kill it. First, Text 2's generalization is universal — 'Every barrage yet built produces less than its pre-construction survey promised' — so it is an objection to barrage estimates as a class, not a case for one site; the narrowness clause grades the shortfall, it does not endorse another site. Second, the stem asks how Text 2 responds to an ESTIMATE, and a site recommendation is not a response to an estimate. Strong distractor, correctly a distractor.

CS2-H-21.note: A is a near-paraphrase of Text 2's closing clause — 'not at all in two reaches where elk numbers fell just as sharply but no dams were built'. All three distractors are flatly contradicted by Text 2 (B invents a wolf-to-beaver mechanism, C denies a premise Text 2 accepts, D reverses the dating Text 2 supplies). The weakest item in the set: one option restates the text and nothing competes.

CS2-H-22.note: Deciding span: 'an evenly spread error rate on held-out material tells you nothing about the error it will make here' — the record is granted and its reach denied. D is the overreach trap (Text 2 attacks the evidence, not the nephew) and is the only one with any pull; A and C are flat.

CS2-H-23.note: Deciding span: 'A patron who once renewed a novel twice contributed three to the print figure and now contributes one to the electronic figure' — an artifact of counting, so the two series are not comparable. A is contradicted by 'the number of distinct borrowers flat across the whole period'; C is absurd; D would grant Text 1's inference.

CS2-H-24.note: Deciding span: 'nothing in the design separates what the parents transmitted from what the site supplied' — D restates it almost verbatim. On the author's doubt: C is NOT a second key, and Text 2's own logic refutes it — 'a coral's heat tolerance is reset within weeks by the temperature swings it has lately met', so a tolerance that belongs to the channel does not travel with a fragment taken out of it; the channels are named as a confound, not a source. passage_needed false: with the stem alone, A is too strong a denial, B is an out-of-scope forecast and C advises rather than responds, leaving D on shape.
